Eligible merchants can use a free self-service workspace to connect their own stores to Shop Direct. Existing Amazon sellers may qualify for selection they do not sell on Amazon.

Google says Google-account users can generate up to three 15-second videos per month in Vids without payment.

TikTok Shop describes shop-specific product recommendations, content assistance and LIVE diagnostics for BFCM preparation. Available agents vary by shop.
DeepSeek lists Flash input/output pricing that varies by peak and off-peak time. Flash supports image input; the listed V4 Pro API does not.
Anthropic lists Sonnet 5.5 at USD 2 per million input tokens and USD 10 per million output tokens, and positions it as a balanced speed/intelligence model.
LinkedIn says it is reducing repetitive low-substance content, engagement bait and inauthentic engagement while improving professional relevance.

reports.title: The AI commerce shift: distribution and creative economics
reports.body_md:
# The AI commerce shift: distribution and creative economics

The first evidence set points to two practical questions: where will AI-mediated shopping send customers, and how cheaply can a seller test accurate creative?

Amazon’s text-shopping invitation rollout and Shop Direct workspace address discovery and purchase. Google’s Omni release and Vids allowance address creative production. These announcements describe access and capabilities; they do not establish seller revenue lift.

For a merchant, the immediate experiment is a small, profitable assortment with accurate product attributes, followed by a controlled creative test. Track contribution per visitor and cost per approved asset. Keep shipping, returns and commissions in the calculation.

At Google’s stated USD 0.07 per second, one 15-second 720p generation has a USD 1.05 generation charge. That excludes revisions, other services and human review. It is not a complete production-cost estimate.

The database starts with nine documents and seven numeric observations. There is no longitudinal baseline yet. Do not infer growth rates, forecast adoption, or compare benchmarks from this bootstrap. Price changes will become measurable after comparable subsequent observations.

Next research questions: which channels are generally available rather than invitation-only; how API prices change under identical billing conditions; whether independent tests reproduce vendor claims; which seller workflows produce measured operating value.
reports.disclosure: AI-assisted research by Signal, created for Ryan Dacus. No individual human-review attestation.
reports.limitations: Purposive nine-document bootstrap; provider statements; no measured adoption, seller outcomes or longitudinal trend.

social_drafts.hook: An AI demo can be impressive. The business question is what changes after the demo.
social_drafts.body:
Amazon is testing shopping by text and expanding a route for eligible merchants’ own catalogs. Google has introduced 15-second video generation with a limited free allowance in Vids.

My research desk is tracking three things: what is available, what it costs, and what independent evidence supports it.

For sellers, the practical test is narrow: one proven product, three creative angles, and contribution per visitor as the outcome.

I’m building a dated evidence library so we can compare these changes over time. This first snapshot establishes a baseline; it does not establish adoption or revenue lift.

AI-assisted research: Signal. Sources accompany the briefing.
social_drafts.hypothesis: A concrete business decision with transparent evidence will attract qualified operator engagement.
